environment.title: Environment variables
environment.description: Variables read by the server, the plugins and Docker Compose (see .env.example). Read-only: change them in .env or in the environment and restart the server.
environment.noneSet: No environment variable is set: the server uses all the defaults.

variables.NOCUMENT_PORT: Port of the web app in production (compose.yaml).
variables.NOCUMENT_DEV_PORT: Port of the web app in development (compose.dev.yaml, Vite dev server).
variables.NOCUMENT_DEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS: Host names, separated by commas, the development web app answers to besides localhost.
variables.MONGODB_DEV_PORT: Port of MongoDB published on 127.0.0.1 in development.
variables.GUNICORN_WORKERS: Number of gunicorn workers (production image only).
variables.MONGODB_URI: MongoDB URI: when set the content blocks are saved in MongoDB, otherwise in the SQLite file.
variables.MONGODB_DATABASE: MongoDB database of the content blocks (only with MONGODB_URI).
variables.NOCUMENT_DATABASE: SQLite file of the content blocks, used when MONGODB_URI is not set.
variables.NOCUMENT_STORAGE: "memory" keeps the content blocks in memory: they are lost when the server restarts.
variables.NOCUMENT_SETTINGS: JSON file of the settings chosen in this page.
variables.NOCUMENT_LOG_LEVEL: Minimum level of the log: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR.
variables.NOCUMENT_LOG_LEVELS: Levels of single loggers, comma separated (e.g. werkzeug=WARNING).
variables.NOCUMENT_LOG_FILE: Log file, rotated by size; empty to log only to the console.
variables.NOCUMENT_LOG_MAX_BYTES: Size of the log file before rotation, in bytes.
variables.NOCUMENT_LOG_BACKUPS: Number of old log files kept.
variables.SOFFICE_PATH: LibreOffice executable; by default searched in the PATH and in the standard folders.
variables.SOFFICE_TIMEOUT: Timeout of a LibreOffice conversion, in seconds.
variables.UNO_PYTHON: Python with LibreOffice's uno module, used to update the tables of contents; by default searched automatically.
variables.NOCUMENT_PLUGIN_UPLOAD: "false" forbids installing and removing plugins from the web app.
variables.AZURE_DEVOPS_URL: URL of the Azure DevOps / TFS collection, required by the plugin.
variables.AZURE_DEVOPS_TOKEN: Personal access token used when the Token field of the plugin is left empty.
variables.NOCUMENT_COMMIT: Git commit of the code, shown in Settings → Version; by default read from git (set by the Docker build).
variables.NOCUMENT_COMMIT_DATE: Date of that commit (ISO 8601); by default read from git.
variables.NOCUMENT_BACKEND_PORT: Port of the development backend (python -m src.app); the Vite /api proxy uses the same one.
variables.NOCUMENT_BACKEND_HOST: Address the development backend listens on.

home.title: Welcome to Nocument
home.subtitle: Compile documents by focusing on the content. Follow the steps below, or jump to a feature.

groups.documents: Build documents from Word files or templates, keep reusable templates and compile the keywords of a document into a PDF.
groups.content: Create, import and organize the reusable blocks of headings, paragraphs, images and tables to insert into the documents.
groups.plugins: Extend Nocument with Python scripts that bring external data into the documents as ready-made contents.

features.builder: Open a Word document or template, explore its structure and insert headings, paragraphs and tables with the template's styles.
features.templates: Browse the saved document templates, search them and create a new document from one in a click.
features.compiler: Upload a Word document, find its keywords, assign texts, images or tables and compile the PDF.
features.addContent: Create a reusable block of contents (headings, paragraphs, images and tables) or import it from Word.
features.exploreContents: Search the saved content blocks by title, description or import file and browse their contents.
features.installedPlugins: See the plugins that bring external data into the documents, what they can create and try them.
features.installPlugin: Add a plugin by uploading its Python script, with drag and drop or the + button.

workflow.title: From template to finished document
workflow.intro: Five steps take you from a Word template to a finished document. Each one opens the page where you do it.

template.title: Define a template
template.text: Define a template in Microsoft Word with the styles of paragraphs, headings and tables, then upload it to Nocument. Define it once, reuse it many times.

components.title: Create reusable components
components.text: Create custom reusable components, or import them from your document repository. A component can be a set of headings, paragraphs and images used across several documents, for example the description of your product or system.

build.title: Assemble the document
build.text: Upload the template and start adding components. You can also edit other Word documents instead of starting from an empty page.

keywords.title: Replace the keywords
keywords.text: Replace any keyword in the document, like <VERSION>, <DATE> or <PRODUCT_NAME>, with text, images or tables.

plugins.title: Bring in external data
plugins.text: Write custom plugins in Python to extract data from external sources, like your task database, and insert it as headings, paragraphs, images or tables.
